title: Argentina names preliminary World Cup squad: Gianluca Prestianni in, Paulo Dybala out
content:
Benfica winger Gianluca Prestianni and Chelsea’s Alejandro Garnacho are among the 55 players included in Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni’s preliminary World Cup squad.

In April, 20-year-old Prestianni was handed a six-match ban by UEFA for homophobic conduct. This occurred during Benfica’s Champions League game against Real Madrid, in which Vinicius Jr. alleged that Prestianni had racially abused him. Prestianni denied that accusation at the time.

Last week, FIFA extended Prestianni’s ban globally, meaning he will miss Argentina’s first two World Cup matches against Algeria and Austria, should he be included in the squad. Jordan are Argentina’s third opponent in Group J.

Scaloni, though, has not ruled out Prestianni at this stage of the pre-World Cup process. Prestianni was a key player during Argentina’s run to the Under-20 World Cup final in October. He has only just broken through to the senior team, with one appearance.

Lionel Messi has also been included, despite the Inter Miami captain not yet confirming he will participate in the tournament.

Not really. Scaloni has given himself plenty to think about though. Argentina has to get younger in several parts of the pitch. The 55-man list features a bevvy of first-time call-ups and young players who are now dreaming of making the final 26-man squad. This list does, however, signal the end of Paulo Dybala’s time with the Argentina national team. He has not featured for his country since 2024.

Hamburg’s Nicolas Capuldo, a former Boca Juniors midfielder, received his first-ever international call-up at the age of 27. Getafe defender Zaid Romero and striker Mateo Pellegrino of Parma also received their first invites under Scaloni.

Perhaps one surprise is the selection of Chelsea attacker Garnacho. The 21-year-old winger is in the midst of a disappointing spell at the club level, but Scaloni has long admired Garnacho’s speed as a change-of-pace option on the flank. Garnacho, for now, appears to still be World Cup-bound.

Just one. Strasbourg forward Joaquin Panichelli was left out as he continues to recover from an anterior cruciate ligament tear in his right knee while on international duty with Argentina in March.

Although Panichelli has only played once for the senior side, he was viewed as an alternative to Argentina’s first-choice strikers Lautaro Martinez and Julian Alvarez.

Scaloni has both the joy and the burden of finding ways to make Messi effective at the age of 38. The Argentina captain has not officially announced his intention to play at his sixth World Cup, but the expectation is that he will be there. Scaloni and Messi are aware Argentina can no longer rely so heavily on the former Barcelona superstar.

Tactically, Argentina is a much more direct and intense side when Messi is not at the forefront of their attack. How Scaloni devises Argentina’s identity at the World Cup will be one of the main stories of the tournament.

Argentina will face Honduras on June 6 at Texas A&M University’s Kyle Field, followed by a game against Iceland at Auburn University’s Jordan-Hare Stadium three days later.
